summary: - **[key4hep/k4FWCore#413](https://github.com/key4hep/k4FWCore/pull/413)** — `OverlayTiming` gains a `RandomMixBackgroundFiles` option. When enabled, each file in a background group is treated as an independent event source and drawn from a shuffled permutation, which is reshuffled once exhausted. Previously, runs overlaying fewer events than there are files only ever saw the first few files of a beam-induced background group.

- **[key4hep/k4ActsTracking#127](https://github.com/key4hep/k4ActsTracking/pull/127)** — Fixes outside-in CKF (`PropagateBackward`) to start at the outermost seed space point; previously the outer seed hits were dropped from the final track. Backward tracks are now reversed to inside-out order and stop at the reference surface. Seed parameters and the magnetic field are now evaluated at the start space point, which also affects the default inside-out seeding.

- **[PandoraPFAOrg/LCContent#33](https://github.com/PandoraPFAOrg/LCContent/pull/33)** — Adds Pandora particle-flow algorithms for the IDEA option 2 detector: ECAL-seeded HCAL clustering, dual-readout correction, PFO creation and forward photon ID. Optional ONNX-based photon ID and satellite-cluster merging are built only with `LCContent_BUILD_ML=ON`. Requires PandoraSDK ≥ 04.00.01.

- **[key4hep/k4geo#669](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/pull/669)** — Adds the first version of the ALFA detector concept for FCC-ee (`ALFA_o1_v00`). It includes a Grainita ECAL barrel driver with its sensitive-detector action, a new rho-phi-theta grid segmentation, an outer tracker, and a steering file.

- **[key4hep/k4geo#674](https://github.com/key4hep/k4geo/pull/674)** — `ALLEGRO_o1_v04` now includes its dimensions, materials and other shared files directly from `ALLEGRO_o1_v03`, keeping only its own HCAL files. This restores consistent silicon-wrapper properties between the two versions and prevents silent divergence like that reported in k4geo#673.

- **[AIDASoft/DD4hep#1706](https://github.com/AIDASoft/DD4hep/pull/1706)** — Fixes volume divisions, which did not assign volume and placement extensions to divided volumes. This caused null-pointer exceptions when traversing the volume hierarchy.

- **[hep-fcc/FCC-config#402](https://github.com/HEP-FCC/FCC-config/pull/402)** — The ALLEGRO digi/reco steering gains a `siDigitizer` option to use the new `VTXdigitizerDetailed` digitiser instead of DDPlanarDigi. Pixel pitches are now read from the compact files; DDPlanarDigi resolutions can still be overridden. Digitiser thresholds and smearing still need tuning.

- **[hep-fcc/FCC-config#407](https://github.com/HEP-FCC/FCC-config/pull/407)** — IDEA_o1_v03 reconstruction gains a `--trackingModel` argument for the GGTF ONNX model and downloads it only if it is missing, writing atomically via a temporary file. Previously every `k4run` re-fetched ~65 MB and required network access.

- **[hep-fcc/k4RecCalorimeter#291](https://github.com/HEP-FCC/k4RecCalorimeter/pull/291)** — `TopoCaloNoisyCells` now stores noise data as an indexed vector held in `CaloCellConstantsSvc`. This is faster, uses less memory and avoids duplication when the tool is configured multiple times. ALLEGRO reconstruction results are unchanged.

- **[key4hep/k4Bench#245](https://github.com/key4hep/k4Bench/pull/245)** — Adds an untimed memory pass (`--memory-events N`) to k4run benchmarks that attributes every heap allocation to its owning Gaudi component. It writes per-event heap snapshots, which the new reco Memory dashboard sections are built on.

- **[key4hep/k4Bench#241](https://github.com/key4hep/k4Bench/pull/241)** — Nightly reconstruction benchmarks now cover ALLEGRO, CLD, IDEA and ILD_FCCee configurations, on Zbb and single-electron samples. Support for fetching external data files into benchmark jobs is added.

- **[hep-fcc/fcc-drs#123](https://github.com/HEP-FCC/fcc-drs/pull/123)** — The Data Request System renames "Production IDs" to "Transformation IDs" to match DIRAC terminology. This covers labels, routes and the activity type, and migrates the database table and column for both SQLite and Postgres.
